title: test(plugin-security): the delegated-organization-membership parity test boots once per posture and asks only the probes it asserts
body:
Fixes #26754

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- **改了什么**:只改一个测试文件。`delegated-organization-membership` 的 parity 测试,由「每个 posture 一个大 `it`」改为「每个 posture 只启动一次栈,三个小 `it`(读、导出、插入)共用」,每个 `it` 只调用它真正断言的探针。产品代码零改动,不发版。
- **为什么改**:这个测试在 CI 分片负载下逼近并越过 vitest 默认的 5 秒超时,已经把 merge queue 的构建踢出队列;每踢一次,排在后面的所有 PR 都要重建。
- **风险与回滚**:风险低。原有 5 条断言逐字保留(非空断言在导出 `it` 里多放一份);对三个探针各做一次变异,都只让对应的那个 `it` 变红。回滚就是 revert 本 PR。
- **先看**:`packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/delegated-organization-membership.test.ts` 里 parity `describe` 的 `beforeAll`/`afterAll` 共享栈与三个 `it`;其次是 `boot()` 新增的 `lifetime` 选项(不加它,共享的引擎会在第一个 `it` 后被文件级 `afterEach` 销毁)。
- **两分钟验证**:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-security exec vitest run src/delegated-organization-membership.test.ts -t 'parity: each probe agrees'`,预期 `Tests  6 passed | 64 skipped (70)`,空闲机器上每个 parity `it` 约 0.1–0.3 秒。
- **需要你做的**:无,席位落地。

## What changes

One file: `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/delegated-organization-membership.test.ts`. No product source, no timeout raised, nothing skipped or quarantined.

- **The `[#25107 · ADR-0090 D10] parity` describe.** Per posture (`group`, `isolated`), one stack is booted and seeded in `beforeAll` and destroyed in `afterAll`. Three `it`s share it, so a failure names the operation:
  - a read: find ⇔ `canReadObject`, find ⇔ the read explanation;
  - an export: find ⇔ `canExport`;
  - an insert: insert ⇔ `canWriteObject` insert. It runs last, being the only one that writes.

  Each `it` asks only the probes it asserts. The old single `it` called `probeAnswers` (nine probes per cell), asserted four of them, and threw the other five away: the four field projections and the update probe. Those five stay pinned, per context and per object, in the two probe describes above it.
- **`boot()` gains `lifetime: 'describe'`.** It hands the engine to the caller's `afterAll` instead of the file's per-test `afterEach`, which would otherwise destroy a shared engine after the first `it`. Every other caller is unchanged (default `'test'`).

### Where the time went (measured before choosing the cut)

This is the old `it`, instrumented in a throwaway copy, alone and warm, at `--maxWorkers=1`, two rounds per posture, on base `0ea90c7a18`:

| share of the old per-posture `it` (411–510 ms) | measured |
|:--|:--|
| boot and seed (engine init and schema sync, seed rows, plugin init and start, `seedForReads`) | **10.4–11.6%** |
| the engine operations (9 finds, 9 inserts) | 15.7–17.6% |
| the probes (81 calls) | **71.4–73.9%** |
| … of which the five probes never asserted | **29.8–31.4%** |
| … of which the read explanation (asserted) | 21.5–23.1% |

So the boot was not the cost, which falsifies the dispatch's mechanism assumption. The parity `it` already booted only once per posture, so sharing a stack alone would save nothing there. The cut that pays is to stop asking for answers the test never reads. Sharing the stack is what lets the three operations become separate `it`s without paying three boots.

### Why one stack per posture is sound

I measured it directly. On one stack per posture, every read-side outcome (find ok, `canReadObject`, `canExport`, explain `allowed`, `canWriteObject` insert) was read for all nine cells, then all nine parity inserts were run, then every outcome was read again. Result: `outcomes-equal=true` on both postures. The rows a find returns did change (`rows-equal=false`, for example `parity_4` appears for `delegated in org_a · qa_account`), but no parity assertion reads rows, only whether an operation is refused. The old `it` already ran later cells' finds after earlier cells' inserts. The insert `it` now runs last, so the read and export `it`s see no parity row at all.

### Assertions, before and after

| | before | after |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `expect(` lines in the parity describe (textual) | 5 | 6 |
| assertions executed per run (two postures) | 74 (= 2 × (9 cells × 4 + 1)) | 76 (= 2 × (19 + 10 + 9)) |
| `it`s in the file | 66 | 70 |

All five original assertion lines are present byte-for-byte (compared modulo indentation, by script; none missing, none reworded). The one added line is the original non-vacuity pin (`expect(refused).toEqual(...)`), repeated in the export `it`, because that `it` runs its own find and would otherwise pass vacuously when run alone.

## Tests

### Timings: the slowest parity `it`, before and after

**The leg.** The card's CI leg was a Test Core shard: turbo `--concurrency=4` × `VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=3` on 4 vCPU, so up to 12 runnable test threads. I approximated it on this 4-vCPU container as the file at `--maxWorkers=3` (`VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=3`) beside **11 pure-CPU `node` busy loops**: 12 runnable threads. Other agents' unlocked work on the box (builds, a dogfood run) came on top, uncontrolled; load average per run is in the logs below. This is a CPU-share approximation, not a real shard.

**Paired: the fair comparison.** The original file (a byte-identical untracked copy of base `0ea90c7a18`'s version, blob `356eb401`) and the new file ran in the **same** vitest invocation, under the same burners, on head `e92c25a1b4`. The two files' unchanged control `it`s ("what the rule leaves alone in the probes") agree within each run, so both saw comparable load.

| run | original: slowest parity `it` | new: slowest parity `it` | speed-up | control `it`, original / new |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|:--|
| 1 | 4,159 ms | 1,857 ms | 2.2× | 2,461 / 3,054 ms |
| 2 | 4,151 ms | 1,523 ms | 2.7× | 2,413 / 2,449 ms |
| 3 | 2,957 ms | 1,045 ms | 2.8× | 1,401 / 1,511 ms |

**Sequential, same leg.** Before on base `0ea90c7a18`, after on head `e92c25a1b4`:

| run | before `group` | before `isolated` | after: slowest of 6 parity `it`s |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|
| 1 | **5,403 ms, timed out** | 4,830 ms | 1,486 ms |
| 2 | 3,843 ms | **5,249 ms, timed out** | 1,690 ms |
| 3 | 4,509 ms | **6,126 ms, timed out** | 1,885 ms |

Before, 3 of 3 sequential runs were red at vitest's 5,000 ms default. Each failing record's stack anchors at the parity `it`'s definition (old line 648), which is how vitest 4's JSON reporter records a timeout. After, 6 of 6 loaded runs (3 sequential, 3 paired) are green, and the slowest parity `it` in any of them is **1,885 ms**. Caveat: the sequential after-runs met a lighter box than the before-runs (their control `it`s ran about 1.5× faster), which is why the paired table above is the comparison to quote.

**Alone** (`--maxWorkers=3`, no burners): before `group` 897 ms and `isolated` 823 ms; after, `group` read / export / insert 315 / 153 / 167 ms and `isolated` 286 / 116 / 115 ms.

### The reshaped `it`s still bite: one-shot mutation check (nothing committed)

The diff changes no product behaviour, so no ablation was owed. To show that none of the three new `it`s is vacuous, I mutated each probe on head `e92c25a1b4` in turn through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (wrap mode: anchor must hit once, write verified on disk, restore verified). The mutation made the probe admit exactly the refused context: `if (context?.onBehalfOf && context?.tenantId === 'org_d') return Promise.resolve(true);` at the top of `SecurityPlugin.canReadObject`, `canExport` and `canWriteObject`, in `security-plugin.ts`. The engine's find and insert do not route through these three entry points.

| mutated probe | marker on disk | red `it`s (both postures) | green `it`s | first failure |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `canReadObject` | 1 | read | export, insert | `delegated in org_d · qa_account: canReadObject ⇔ find: expected true to be false` |
| `canExport` | 1 | export | read, insert | `delegated in org_d · qa_account: canExport ⇔ find (an export reads as a find): expected true to be false` |
| `canWriteObject` | 1 | insert | read, export | `delegated in org_d · qa_account: canWriteObject insert ⇔ insert: expected true to be false` |

After each leg: `ok restored: blob == HEAD (fe67e27b8705) and git diff HEAD is empty`, and the marker count went back to 0. A first attempt was a **no-op**: its replacement re-contained the anchor, the tool refused before measuring ("the anchor count moved 1 -> 1"), and it was re-anchored and re-run as above.

### Package suite and typecheck (head `e92c25a1b4`)

- `vitest run --maxWorkers=3` over the whole package: `Test Files  231 passed (231)`, `Tests  5036 passed | 45 skipped (5081)`.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-security typecheck`: exit 0, ending `check:test-typecheck: OK — @objectstack/plugin-security's test layer compiles under packages/plugins/plugin-security/tsconfig.test.json`. That program lists this file (`tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFiles`: 1 hit, 231 test files).
- `pnpm exec eslint packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/delegated-organization-membership.test.ts`: exit 0, no output.
- Not run locally, left to CI: the root `test:repo` project.

## Acceptance notes

- **Dispatch mechanism assumptions, measured.** (1) "The cost is the per-posture boot plus seeding" is **falsified**: about 10% of the `it`; the probes are about 72%, and a third of the `it` was probes it never asserted. (2) "Sharing is safe only if the insert does not change what the read and the export see": the insert changes the rows a later find returns, but no asserted outcome. The isolation here is by order (the one writing `it` runs last), not by distinct rows: the parity cells must cover the same three objects.
- **Observation, not filed.** With the parity `it`s fixed, the slowest `it`s left in this file are the three "what the rule leaves alone in the probes" admitted-probe `it`s, each running `probeAnswers` over three objects. On the same leg they reached 1.9–3.9 s before and 1.5–3.1 s after, under 5 s in every run. They are outside this card, and nothing observed here failed.
- **No changeset.** `files[]` is `dist`, `README.md` and `CHANGELOG.md`. After `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-security build`, this diff's symbols (`parityContexts`, `lifetime: 'describe'`, the new `it` titles) have 0 hits in those paths, while the positive controls (`canExport(`, `delegatedOrganizationRefusal`) hit 4 files each. Nothing publishes. Per the dispatch, the `skip-changeset` label is the seat's to apply; I did not apply it.
- **Base sync.** `origin/main` (then `8eef9a8db4`) was merged in at `e92c25a1b4` before every reading above. Upstream moved code on the measured path: the objectql validate split, a driver-sql move, and #26801's explain-another-user existence check. The last runs only when `request.userId` names another user, and the parity read passes none. The 9 commits that landed since touch nothing under `packages/plugins/plugin-security`, and neither in-flight plugin-security PR the claim named had landed (`git log 0ea90c7a18..origin/main`, with a control commit found in the same range).

## Verification

The gate union ran on head **`e92c25a1b4`** (`git rev-parse --short HEAD`), the head of this PR. It used the list re-derived on that head with no paths, `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`: 52 commands, identical to the pre-merge derivation. Each exit code was captured before any pipe.

- 50 exited 0, each printing its own pass line.
- 2 exited 3 with `PREREQUISITE NOT MET`: **NOT MEASURED** locally, not a pass and not a fail. `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` needs every package's `dist/` (56 absent in this worktree). `check:i18n` needs the CLI's compiled `i18n extract` and its config closure. Both run in CI's `Lint & Repo Gates`, and neither reads a test file.
- Reconciliation, `dispatch-gates --ran` over the recorded `COMMAND :: exit CODE` lines: `52 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 50 run, 2 NOT-MEASURED (2 DERIVED from a recorded exit 3)`.
